conventions.convention: Batch indices start at 1; diagonal image/text pairs are designated matches. Image-to-text probabilities normalize rows and text-to-image probabilities normalize columns. The loss averages the two directional mean negative natural logarithms.
Encoder outputs being normalized must be nonzero; the shared score is a Euclidean inner product multiplied by s = exp(τ) > 0. The indexed batch is nonempty, including N = 1.

Normalize each prompt embedding, average those embeddings within each class, then normalize the average. Class and template lists are finite and nonempty, class descriptions are distinct, and each class average must be nonzero. Score ties return the least class index.

Individual-text retrieval ranks individual prompt embeddings, whereas classification ranks averaged class prototypes. Finite 0–1 error is the total probability mass of misclassified labelled inputs; source and target retain the same labels at each image.

load_bearing.statement: For an indexed nonempty batch of designated image/text pairs with nonzero encoder outputs, normalize the embeddings, use logits ℓij = exp(τ)〈ui,vj〉, and define the symmetric loss as one half the sum of the row-normalized and column-normalized mean diagonal negative log probabilities.

For admissible inputs, form normalized class prototypes by averaging normalized prompt embeddings and renormalizing; compute scaled inner-product scores and softmax probabilities; return the probability vector and the least-index class maximizing the score. The procedure makes no accuracy or distribution-generalization guarantee.

published_dependencies.used_for: Defines the real exponential used for the positive logit scale and softmax terms.
Supplies positivity and the positive-real range of the exponential, ensuring nonzero finite softmax denominators.
Defines the natural logarithm on positive reals, the domain required by the directional loss terms.

concerns.concern: The empirical description gives ViT-L/14@336px as the default model but omits the model exception for the §5 overlap accuracy measurements. Radford et al., §5, printed p. 17, procedure step 2 explicitly uses CLIP RN50x64 for All/Clean/Overlap accuracies. Add that qualifier to the overlap paragraph so the reported accuracy changes cannot be read as ViT-L/14@336px results. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.00020.
